the Kano questionnaire and direct classification are the only methods that can be used in the product/service design stage to identify the Kano quality elements of a product/service; the IG and qualitative data methods are not recommended for this purpose; the PRCA can be used to identify the Kno elements of a product/ service, but its application to the classification of the Kano attributes in this stage of the product/service development process is questionable; the PRCA and qualitative methods can also be used to classify K

the Kano questionnaire and direct classification are the most valid and reliable techniques for classifying attributes in the KANO model, and that PRCA is the most valid and useful technique for evaluating the impact of attributes on customer satisfaction.
the Kano questionnaire and direct classification are the only methods that can accurately classify quality attributes in the design phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the classification of attributes in the KANO model.
the question of whether the classification of quality elements according to the KANO model is a valid and reliable approach.
the question “How can we classify quality attributes in the design phase of a new product/service according to the KANO model?”
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Kano questionnaire is the most appropriate method for classifying attributes in the design and/or development stage of a product or service.
the Kano model is a powerful tool, which is applicable to both product and service design and development.
the Kano questionnaire and PRCA are the most appropriate approaches for classifying Kano quality attributes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the context of the Kano classification of product/service attributes, PRCA and IG should be avoided, while the Kano questionnaire, direct classification, critical incident technique and analysis of complaints/complements should be used with care.
, in the context of the Kano quality model, it is not the objective performance that is important but the subjective performance perception of the consumer.
the Kano questionnaire is the best method for classifying attributes in the KANO model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kano model should be applied in a way that is consistent with the original conceptualisation of the model.
researchers should be careful in their interpretation of the Kano classification of attributes and should not rely on the results of a single technique.
the Kano questionnaire is a valid and reliable method for classifying attributes in the KANO model.
